svg.text: Clark's line through III:24–27: what the critique attacks, and what it keeps
attacked: the value of truth
kept: truth, and its own truth-claims
the unconditional value: "nothing is more needful
than truth, all else of the second rank" (GS 344)
that some beliefs are true and others false: the
experiment on truth's value needs true beliefs to run
truth "as being, as God, as highest court",
"not permitted to be a problem" (§24)
"the lie in the belief in God" (§27): the atheist's
finding is accepted as what it is, a truth found
the faith in truth's "inestimability and
uncriticizability" shared by science and ideal (§25)
"we knowers" (§24; Preface 1): the Genealogy's own
claims, offered as true by a will to truth
the unquestioned assumption that "being scientific"
is the overriding ideal for a person (Clark on GS 344)
"so much the better" (BGE 22): a claim offered as one
more interpretation is still offered, and ranked
truth pursued "for its own sake": knowledge as an
autonomous value (§24's "last idealists")
the commitment to truth in another ideal's service:
"the service of truth is the hardest service" (A 50)
what the critique needs to replace it: a counter-ideal
for the will to truth to serve (§25)
"how much truth can a spirit endure?": the measure
of value after the faith is gone (EH Preface 3)
the critique turns on the value of truth, not on truth: a genealogy of the will to truth is itself a truth-claim
Clark, ch. 6 §§4–5; the radical reading takes the left column's "value of truth" for the right column's "truth"
